jobs.title: Humanties teacher (Part time )
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you seeking a flexible, part-time teaching role that fits seamlessly around your current commitments?

Are you ready to start a rewarding new teaching contract immediately?

Are you passionate about guiding students of all abilities to achieve their full academic potential?

About the Role

This is an exciting opportunity for a dedicated Part-Time Humanities Teacher to join a vibrant educational department on an immediate basis. The successful candidate will deliver engaging, high-quality lessons across Humanities subjects (including History, Geography, and Religious Studies) to students across Key Stages 3 and 4.

The role is offered on a part-time basis, providing the ideal balance between professional fulfilment and personal flexibility. The successful applicant will step into a well-structured framework, taking responsibility for inspiring pupils, managing classroom dynamics positively, and assessing student progress to drive academic achievement.

About the School

Situated in Bradford, this highly regarded school is built on a foundation of inclusive values, community spirit, and high academic expectations. The institution prides itself on creating a warm, safe, and stimulating environment where both pupils and staff are encouraged to flourish.With a strong ethos centred on mutual respect, personal development, and moral responsibility, the school maintains a broad curriculum designed to nurture well-rounded, compassionate global citizens. Staff benefit from a supportive leadership team and modern classroom facilities designed to enhance teaching and learning across all key stages.

Key Requirements

  • Qualified Teacher Status (QTS): Holds QTS, QTLS, or an equivalent recognised UK teaching qualification.
  • Enhanced DBS: A valid Enhanced DBS clearance registered on the Update Service (or a willingness to apply for one).
  • References: Provision of full, verifiable professional references covering the last 2 years.
  • Eligibility to Work: Valid legal entitlement to work full-time in the UK.

Essential Skills

  1. Engaging Pedagogy: Ability to turn complex historical, geographical, and social concepts into captivating lessons.
  2. Strong Communication: Excellent verbal and written skills for clear delivery, constructive feedback, and staff/parent engagement.
  3. Adaptability: Flexibility to step into an active timetable smoothly and adjust lessons to real-time classroom dynamics.
  4. Digital Literacy: Proficiency with educational technology, interactive whiteboards, and digital learning tools.
  5. Time Management: Exceptional organisation to handle lesson planning, marking, and reporting within part-time hours.
  6. Empathy & Patience: Deep commitment to supporting children's emotional and academic development.

Core Responsibilities

  1. Lesson Delivery: Plan, prepare, and deliver high-quality, differentiated Humanities lessons across Key Stages 3 and 4 in line with curriculum guidelines.
  2. Student Assessment: Monitor, record, and assess student progress regularly, offering constructive oral and written feedback to drive improvement.
  3. Classroom Management: Establish and maintain a safe, orderly, and positive classroom environment using constructive behaviour management strategies.
  4. Curriculum Enhancement: Adapt teaching resources and learning materials to cater to a diverse range of learning styles and academic abilities.
  5. Safeguarding: Uphold strict safeguarding and child protection standards at all times to promote student welfare.
  6. Parental Communication: Attend parent's evenings and prepare clear, accurate academic reports to keep families informed of pupil achievement.
  7. Departmental Collaboration: Collaborate with colleagues in the Humanities department to share best practices, update schemes of work, and plan resources.
  8. Inclusion & Support: Tailor learning strategies to support pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and English as an Additional Language (EAL).
  9. Professional Development: Engage in internal training sessions, INSET days, and performance reviews to continuously refine teaching practice.
  10. School Ethos Integration: Act as a positive role model, actively supporting and embedding the core values and code of conduct of the school.

What We Offer:

  • A supportive, collaborative working environment.
  • Opportunities for career progression and ongoing professional development.
  • The chance to make a significant impact on the lives of students.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • A Refer a Friend scheme where you could earn a £300 Love2shop voucher (subject to terms and conditions).

Could this be the ideal role for you?
Click "Apply Now" to submit your application for the role of a Humanities Teacher. For more information, please contact or call to speak to the secondary team.

jobs.title: Service Coordinator Part time
jobs.description:
Job Description

Service Coordinator £14.46 - £16.37 per hour 18.5 hours per week | 6-month fixed-term contract | Hybrid/flexible working We're recruiting for a Service Coordinator to join a not-for-profit organisation based in Bradford, supporting its Children and Young People (CYP) services. This is a 6-month fixed-term role, with the possibility of extending depending on service requirements . You'll provide important operational and administrative support during a period of workforce transition, vacancies and staff absence, helping to keep things running smoothly across the service. What will you be doing? As a Service Coordinator, you'll support a range of operational processes, including: Completing case file audits, file closure reviews and service activity spot checks. Maintaining audit records and following up on outstanding actions. Supporting accurate record keeping and compliance with service procedures. Monitoring incidents and safeguarding concerns, ensuring actions are followed up and recorded appropriately. Maintaining incident and safeguarding trackers and escalating overdue actions where needed. Monitoring referrals, caseloads and waiting lists across CYP services. Keeping databases, records and trackers accurate and up to date. Supporting data quality checks and producing routine operational reports. Coordinating staff rotas, cover arrangements and workforce records. What are we looking for? You'll need previous experience in an administrative, coordination or operational support role, along with: Maintaining databases, trackers and records. Producing reports and monitoring information. Spporting quality assurance or audit processes. Knowledge of safeguarding within children's, health, social care or voluntary sector settings. Strong organisational and IT skills. Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities. Confidence using databases, spreadsheets and reporting systems. Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively across different teams. You'll be organised, reliable and comfortable keeping on top of several priorities at once. This is a role where accuracy, follow-through and good communication are important. What's on offer? Flexible/hybrid working in line with service requirements . 6-month fixed-term contract, with potential to extend. 25 days' annual leave, increasing to 28 days with length of service, plus bank holidays (pro rata). Up to two additional wellbeing days each year. Simply Health Cash Plan, including support towards dental, optical, prescriptions and physiotherapy costs. Employee Assistance Service with 24/7 confidential mental health support and access to structured therapy sessions. Generous pension scheme and employer contribution. Discount schemes including Company Shop and Blue Light Card. Personal development opportunities, including access to Clinical Supervision. Enhanced sick pay after six-month probation. Accredited employer with Mindful Employer, Disability Confident and Real Living Wage
